title: How Phone Scams Actually Work — Two True US Stories

episode.title: "The $400,000 Machine: How US Phone Scams Are Actually Built"
episode.description: "Two true stories. One machine. How the grandparent bail call and the fake trading app are built — the call centers, the spoofed numbers, the innocent couriers, and the one question that stops all of it."

rows.vo: "Seventy-two thousand. That's how many times Americans pick up this exact kind of call, every single day. And every one of those calls was built."

beats.name: THE ASSEMBLY LINE (0:00)

beats.name: THE COURIER (0:00)

rows.vo: "Then comes the part that should break it open. A courier arrives to pick up the cash. In person. He could be caught. But he's not a criminal — technically. In the real cases, the men who showed up thought they were collecting legal documents. The app that hired them was run by the scammers: fake business name, fake address, and a real payment processor that approved it."

beats.name: THE ONE QUESTION (0:00)

rows.vo: "Here's the test. Ask a question only your family could answer. 'Which Mikey? I have two grandsons.' The line goes dead. Because the machine sells panic — and a question is a firewall."

beats.name: THE DEFENSE (0:00)

rows.vo: "That's why the defense is one sentence: hang up, and call the number on the back of the card. Not the number they gave you. The one on the card. Every call has a flaw, and the spoofed number is it. You never have to outsmart them. You just have to be willing to be rude to someone who sounds desperate."

beats.name: THE KINDNESS PROBLEM (0:00)

rows.vo: "The scam isn't a technology problem. It's a kindness problem. The IRS never calls. No judge takes cash. And your grandson's voice, in a panic, is the one sound the human brain was never designed to question."
